title: add webrtc workload runners, profiling baselines, and reporting pipeline
author: Aisha Patel
description: Add WebRTC representative workload runners, profiling baselines for cold/start and steady-state scenarios, and a reporting pipeline to ingest results into the benchmark dashboard. Motivation: we have received multiple requests from product teams to measure real-time/video-chat style workloads (low-latency token generation with frequent short-turns) and existing text-only runners do not capture queueing / small-batch latency behavior. This PR introduces: 1) a set of WebRTC-style workload runners (python) that simulate concurrent peer connections, short prompt lengths, and intermittent audio-transcription style traffic; 2) profiling baselines YAMLs for cold-start, warm steady-state, and KV-cache-heavy sessions; 3) an Airflow reporting DAG that normalizes runner outputs, computes p50/p90/p99 latency histograms and token-cost summaries, and uploads to the benchmark-lab metrics store. Checklist: - [x] runner implementation and unit tests - [x] profiling baseline documents - [x] reporting DAG and transformer - [x] basic e2e smoke validated on staging - [x] docs (how to run & interpret) - [x] Linear ticket(s) referenced. Notes: The reporting DAG uses existing S3->BigQuery committer used by other benchmark runners and reuses the same schema. This change is additive and non-breaking to existing pipelines. Related: ENG-4211, PM-998.
